name: spandsp
why: A telephony DSP library covering modems and fax tones, a real door into how old modem signals are built and decoded.

brief.what_it_is: spandsp is a library of digital signal processing functions for telephony, aimed at the 8000 samples-per-second world of E1, T1 and higher-order PCM channels. It spans low-level pieces such as basic filters up to higher-level ones such as cadenced supervisory tone detection and a complete software FAX machine. It is a library for other programs to call, not a standalone app. The README being read is for version 3.1.1.
brief.why_it_exists: The README does not give a separate motivation. It stresses that the code was written to avoid intellectual property problems by using mature techniques whose relevant patents have expired.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. It says the library operates on 8000-sample-per-second telephony audio and uses techniques from mature, patent-expired work.
brief.install_notes: The README lists dependencies. libtiff (and libtiff-devel on most Linux distributions) is required to build the spandsp library. The test suite additionally needs libaudiofile (and libaudiofile-devel) and fftw (and fftw-devel); FFTW version 2 or 3 both work. The optional GUI parts of the test suite need fltk (and fltk-devel), plus Fl_Cartesian and Fl_Audio_Meter, which the README says come from http://www.soft-switch.org/downloads. The tests build without the GUI packages. No install commands appear in the README.
brief.standout: Its design goal is stated openly as avoiding patent trouble by building on techniques whose patents have expired. It also bundles a full software fax machine and tone detection into one telephony-focused DSP library, which is unusual for a library of this size.
brief.status: Version 3.1.1 is named in the README. I found no release date, last-commit date or maintenance note in what I fetched, so the status is unknown. The author is listed as Steve Underwood. The repository I read is the freeswitch/spandsp mirror on GitHub.
brief.caveats: The homepage https://www.soft-switch.org/ returned unrelated spam content (an Indonesian gambling-site product page), not spandsp documentation, so I could not confirm anything from it. The scout note mentions modems, but the README I read says only fax and tone detection, not modems. The GitHub URL under steveu/spandsp returned 404, so I used the freeswitch mirror. The README also points to a DueDiligence file on IP issues and a COPYING file for licence text, which I did not fetch. Licensing is LGPL 2.1 for the library and GPL 2 for the test suite and support programs.
quotes: SpanDSP is a library of DSP functions for telephony, in the 8000 sample per second world of E1s, T1s, and higher order PCM channels.
The software has been designed to avoid intellectual property issues, using mature techniques where all relevant patents have expired.
It also contains higher level functions, such as cadenced supervisory tone detection, and a complete software FAX machine.
